sections.heading: why_in_hospital
sections.text:
You came in with chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion.

The team found you had:
- A heart attack (NSTEMI)
- Severe narrowing in three of the arteries supplying your heart

The team looked at your arteries and decided, after a team discussion, that an operation to open them up (PCI) was not suitable for you. They treated you with medicines instead.

sections.heading: what_we_did
sections.text:
While you were in hospital, the team:
- Did a heart tracing (ECG)
- Took blood tests to check your heart and kidneys
- Did a camera test of your heart arteries (coronary angiogram)

They treated you with:
- A blood-thinning injection (fondaparinux)
- A new antiplatelet medicine (ticagrelor), used alongside your existing antiplatelet medicine
- An increased dose of a heart medicine (bisoprolol), now 7.5mg once daily
- A new medicine for chest pain (isosorbide mononitrate) 30mg once daily
- Exercises with a physiotherapist to help you move around
- A referral to cardiac rehabilitation

sections.heading: medicines
sections.text: {{MEDICATIONS}}

sections.heading: next_steps
sections.text:
- You have a cardiology outpatient appointment in 6 weeks.
- Your GP will check your kidney function and may adjust your ACE inhibitor medicine as your body tolerates it.
